clause: PDMRs are prohibited from dealing ... where the dealing involves transactions in put options, call options or other derivative securities, on an exchange or in any other organised market
why_it_matters: A bilateral OTC collar with a bank is outside the express ban, so its treatment turns on the dealing definition and clearance, but the bank should not hedge or novate the position through listed options in the executive's name.

clause: BHP will take a substance over form approach and will have regard to the intent and spirit of this policy when applying and enforcing it.
why_it_matters: A Clearance Officer may treat an OTC collar as within the spirit of the exchange-traded derivatives ban or the hedging ban and refuse clearance on that basis.

clause: An investment with a maturity of one year or less is considered of a short-term nature
why_it_matters: Both the collar and the loan must have a tenor exceeding twelve months for a PDMR, and early termination or roll features may be scrutinised.

clause: Participants must not at any time enter into a transaction that operates or is intended to operate to limit participants' exposure to the risk of holding unvested BHP securities ... or vested BHP securities that are subject to holding locks or similar restrictions.
why_it_matters: Only vested shares free of holding locks or plan restrictions can be collared; the ban applies at any time, including outside Closed Periods, and is intent-based.

clause: Dealing includes ... use as security, or otherwise granting a charge, lien or other encumbrance over securities ... entry into any margin lending or other secured financing arrangement.
why_it_matters: The loan leg and the security interest over the collared shares each require clearance and are barred in Closed Periods, and for PDMRs are publicly disclosed via FCA and exchange notification.

clause: If the market was aware of all the current circumstances, could the proposed dealing be perceived as taking advantage of my position in an inappropriate way? ... clearance will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the considerations above.
why_it_matters: Clearance for a director's collar is discretionary and may be refused on perception grounds even absent inside information.

clause: Upon receipt of written approval, the dealing must be completed within two business days. ... A clearance to deal can be withdrawn if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances.
why_it_matters: The collar and loan must be priced and signed within two business days of clearance, and BHP can withdraw clearance before execution.

clause: PDMRs must ensure that their PCAs: must request clearance before dealing in BHP securities ... companies, trusts, partnerships or entities: which are managed by a PDMR or a family member; which are directly or indirectly controlled by a PDMR
why_it_matters: A collar or loan entered through a family trust or controlled company needs the same clearance and disclosure as if entered by the PDMR.

clause: exceptional circumstances, such as severe financial difficulty or compulsion by court order, exist which require the immediate sale of shares
why_it_matters: Closed Period relief covers an immediate sale, not entry into a hedge or financing, and the policy is silent on a lender's enforcement sale in a Closed Period.

topic: dealing on behalf of a third party
clause: Persons on insider lists, Restricted Persons, PDMRs and their PCAs must not deal (or deal on behalf of a third party) in BHP securities during any Closed Period.
why_it_matters: Physical settlement, unwind or collateral top-up during a Closed Period would be a dealing; structures should cash-settle or avoid mandatory delivery dates in Closed Periods.

clause: Specified Persons and their Associates must not use Group Securities as security for margin lending or other secured financing arrangements, as a forced sale may lead to the breach of this Policy.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar secured on the collared shares is expressly prohibited for every Specified Person, and there is no secured-lender-sale exception if the bank enforces.

clause: Para 8 bans risk-limiting transactions on unvested or locked plan securities for all Specified Persons; para 9 extends the ban to any vested Group Securities only for CBA Board directors, Group Company Secretaries, Group Executives and their Associates.
why_it_matters: The hedge leg is available only to Specified Persons outside the para 9 group (e.g. Executive General Managers, Subsidiary Board directors) and only over vested shares free of any holding lock.

clause: Trading involving conditional or limit orders (e.g. a specified, minimum sell or maximum purchase price or a stop-loss instruction) must be placed and executed during a Trading Window.
why_it_matters: A collar whose put or call is exercised or physically settled at maturity, or any price-triggered unwind, may execute outside a Trading Window and breach the policy unless cash-settled or timed to a window.

clause: Off-market transfers with no change in beneficial ownership are exempt from Trading Windows other than those by the CBA Board directors and their Associates.
why_it_matters: A director transferring collared shares to a bank custodian or security account is making a Trade that must occur in a Trading Window with Pre-Clearance.

clause: A Trading Window exception must be requested in writing with evidence that the proposed Trade is the most reasonable course of action and there are no other viable legal alternatives; it remains in force for seven calendar days unless revoked earlier, Pre-Clearance if required must be obtained within that period, Group Control Room must be notified, and confirmation of whether the Trade was placed must go to the approver and Group Control Room by the next business day.
why_it_matters: The hardship relief is drafted around a sale and does not extend to entering a hedge, so a collar cannot be executed in a closed period under it.

clause: CBA Board directors, Group Company Secretaries, Group Executives and Associates must not Trade any other Security that has a price or value which depends on, or has an effect on, the price or value of a Group Security that is listed or traded on a UK or EU regulated market.
why_it_matters: If the collar's reference security or any Group Security it prices off is listed on a UK or EU market, the derivative is barred outright for this group regardless of Trading Windows.

clause: The prohibition on Insider Trading applies at all times and overrides any Pre-Clearance, exception or other provision of this Policy. Pre-Clearance or an exception being granted is not an endorsement of any Trade.
why_it_matters: Pre-Clearance does not protect the executive or the bank if the executive holds Inside Information when the collar is struck.

clause: If Group Securities make up 20% or more of an exchange traded fund (ETF) at the time of placing a Trade, the ETF is considered to be a Group Security for the purposes of this Policy.
why_it_matters: A hedge referenced to a CBA-heavy ETF is treated as a hedge of Group Securities.

clause: The Specified Person list is not exhaustive and other individuals may be considered Specified Persons; designation is recorded on the Conflicts Hub and may change from time to time.
why_it_matters: The bank should confirm the counterparty's current designation and whether they fall in the para 9 group before structuring, since the answer differs between tiers.

clause: If Pre-Clearance requirements apply to you, you should refer to the Procedure for further information including how to seek Pre-Clearance and for which types of Trading it is required.
why_it_matters: Whether an OTC derivative specifically requires Pre-Clearance is settled by the unpublished Procedure, not this policy.

clause: the Derivative must have a maturity date that falls within the eight-week period that immediately follows the date on which either NAB's half-year or full-year financial results are released to the ASX
why_it_matters: The collar's put and call must both expire within eight weeks after a results release, which fixes the available tenors (roughly six or twelve months from an open window) and rules out long-dated or open-ended structures.

clause: neither NAB nor any member of the Group can be a counterparty to the Derivative.
why_it_matters: The collar and, prudently, the loan must be written by a bank outside the NAB Group; NAB's own markets desk cannot face the executive.

clause: Derivatives may be used by NAB People in relation to those vested securities in the following circumstances: to protect the value of an asset supporting a loan taken out for the exercise price of options granted by NAB; to protect the value of the Group Security where the employee has paid or is required to pay a tax liability at the tax cessation time; or on a case-by-case basis with approval
why_it_matters: A general funded collar falls outside the two self-executing purposes and needs discretionary case-by-case approval (Chair for Directors, Group Company Secretary for the Chair, Group CEO or delegate for ELT and others) in addition to the Compliance Certificate.

clause: Group Securities are considered vested once the NAB-imposed time and performance hurdles have been satisfied, irrespective of whether a NAB Person has opted for a longer period of restriction
why_it_matters: Shares under a voluntary extended holding lock are collar-eligible, but for KMP shares that remain subject to forfeiture conditions after vesting are still off limits under 3.5.5.

clause: Margin Loan: A loan arrangement whereby NAB Securities are mortgaged, provided as security, lent, or charged to a financier.
why_it_matters: The bank loan secured on the collared shares is a Margin Loan regardless of label, so Directors and ELT must lodge a Compliance Certificate before drawdown and before any collateral top-up.

clause: NAB will publicly disclose all Derivative positions over Group Securities taken out by a Director or by Key Management Personnel of the Group ... irrespective of whether or not the particular form of Derivative technically falls within the disclosure requirements of the ASX Listing Rules or the Corporations Act.
why_it_matters: A Director's or ELT member's collar will be announced to the market and reported in the Annual Financial Report even if it would not otherwise be notifiable, so confidentiality of the structure cannot be assumed.

clause: Directors and members of the Executive Leadership Team are required to inform the Group Company Secretary where a financier demands payment under a Margin Loan and there is a risk that the demand will not be able to be satisfied without the disposal of Group Securities.
why_it_matters: Any loan-to-value breach or margin call on the funded collar may have to be escalated internally and potentially disclosed to the market; the policy is silent on whether a forced sale in a Black-out Period is a breach.

clause: Acknowledgment of the Compliance Certificate by NAB is intended as a compliance monitoring function only, and is not an endorsement of the proposed transaction.
why_it_matters: The certificate is a no-inside-information confirmation acknowledged by the Chair or manager rather than a substantive approval, and the Trade must occur within 5 business days of acknowledgement.

clause: Performance rights must only be exercised outside the Black-out Periods.
why_it_matters: Shares to be collared must be settled from exercise outside the roughly six-week Black-out Periods beginning 16 March and 16 September, and the collar itself as a Trade in Derivatives is likewise confined to open periods.

clause: Must not: Means an action is explicitly prohibited and any deviation from this will require a formal policy exemption.
why_it_matters: Written exemptions are available only in Exceptional Circumstances (hardship or legal compulsion to sell), so they cannot be used to permit a collar over unvested or forfeitable securities.

clause: If your margin lender sells any of your Westpac securities during a Blackout Period, whether on your instructions to do so or not, it will be considered a breach of this Policy.
why_it_matters: Enforcement or physical settlement of the collared shares by the bank during the 15 March or 15 September Blackout Periods puts the Director or executive in breach even if involuntary, so the facility must not permit lender sales in those windows.

clause: Westpac securities cannot be sold to meet a margin call during a Blackout Period or if you are in receipt of inside information relating to Westpac.
why_it_matters: Any loan-to-value shortfall on the funded collar must be met in cash or other assets during Blackout Periods or while the executive holds inside information.

clause: If a Westpac Director or Prescribed Employee has any doubt about their ability to meet a margin call by means other than a sale of their Westpac securities, they should take steps to rearrange their affairs to have a facility that does not contain price triggers (for example, an investment loan secured against other assets).
why_it_matters: A collar with a put floor can support a loan without price triggers, which aligns with the policy's stated preference, but a facility with LTV triggers requires demonstrable alternative resources.

topic: change of ownership is a trade
clause: Any transaction which causes a change in ownership of Westpac securities will be considered a trade of securities under this Policy. This includes a transfer to a family member, family trust or personal superannuation scheme.
why_it_matters: Moving collared shares into a lender's nominee or a sponsored holding may itself be a trade needing notification or Chairman approval and must occur outside Blackout Periods.

clause: buy or sell Westpac securities, or entering into a hedging arrangement over vested Westpac securities; or arrange for another person to enter into arrangements of those kinds.
why_it_matters: The collar is expressly recognised as a permissible hedging arrangement over vested securities, subject to the tier's approval or notification and Blackout Periods, and the arranging limb catches hedges placed through associates or the bank.

clause: In addition, Key Prescribed Employees are subject to the requirements as set out in the Key Prescribed Employee Trading Process, which is an Addendum to this Policy.
why_it_matters: For senior executives the operative pre-clearance terms (approver, validity, conditions) sit in an unpublished addendum that must be obtained before structuring.

clause: any trustee of a trust or other fiduciary arrangement under which you, your spouse or partner or your dependent children, is or may be a beneficiary; any company in which you hold (directly or indirectly) a majority of the shares or otherwise control
why_it_matters: A collar or loan written to a family trust or controlled company is treated as the executive's own trade unless the executive is fully excluded from the decision.

clause: The Chief Compliance Officer has discretion to extend or reduce (conditionally or unconditionally) the Blackout Periods.
why_it_matters: Open windows are not fixed; collar entry, roll or unwind dates must be confirmed with the Group Control Room close to execution.

clause: Westpac Directors must also notify the General Manager, Company Secretary immediately of any trading by either themselves or their associates in Westpac securities including entering into a hedging arrangement over vested Westpac securities.
why_it_matters: A Director's collar will be notified to the Company Secretary immediately and reported to ASX under Listing Rule 3.19A, so the structure will be public.

clause: not use ANZ Securities in connection with a margin loan or similar financing arrangements that may be subject to a margin call or loan to value ratio;
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar secured on the collared shares with any LTV covenant or margin call right is prohibited outright for Directors, ExCo, KMP and all other Restricted Persons and their Associates; only a facility with no margin call or LTV mechanism falls outside the literal ban.

topic: hedging ban extends to locked and clawback shares
clause: an unvested holding or a holding subject to a holding lock or clawback period under an ANZ employee or executive incentive plan
why_it_matters: Vested deferred or restricted shares cannot be collared until both the holding lock and any clawback period have expired; only unencumbered plan shares or on-market purchases are eligible.

clause: any transaction or change affecting title to or interest in ANZ Securities or ANZ Rights
why_it_matters: Granting a charge, transferring shares to a lender's nominee, and each put/call leg are all Trades requiring Pre-trade Approval outside Blackout Periods, and unwinds or settlements need fresh approval.

clause: outside of Blackout Periods, a transfer of ANZ Securities from a Broker Account held solely in the name of the ANZ Restricted Person and/ or Associate to another Broker Account held in the ANZ Restricted Person and/ or Associate's own name.
why_it_matters: Only same-name transfers are exempt from Pre-trade Approval; moving collared shares into a bank custody or nominee account is a Trade needing approval, and the August 2026 update was specifically made to tighten controls on off-market transfers.

clause: Employees and contingent workers must not engage in Trading in ANZ Securities where the proposed Trade could be perceived as taking advantage of their position.
why_it_matters: Even a technically compliant collar can be refused or later criticised if it could be seen as exploiting the executive's position, giving approvers a broad discretionary veto.

clause: Blackout Periods commence: Two months prior to the announcement of ANZ's half year and full year financial results; Two weeks prior to any periodic ANZ market trading updates
why_it_matters: Roughly five to six months of each year are closed, plus trading-update and ad hoc blackouts, so collar entry, rolls, resets and unwinds must be scheduled into narrow open windows.

clause: Pre-trade Approvals are valid for 48 hours. Limit orders which have not been executed within 48 hours require a new Pre-trade Approval.
why_it_matters: The collar must be priced and executed within 48 hours of approval, and approval lapses if the executive receives Inside Information before execution.

clause: ANZ Restricted Persons must treat their Associates' transactions for the purpose of this Policy and applicable laws as if the transactions were their own.
why_it_matters: Structuring the collar or loan through a spouse, SMSF, trust or controlled company does not avoid the financing ban or approval requirements.

clause: Acknowledgement of a Pre-trade Approval by or on behalf of ANZ is intended as a compliance monitoring function only and is not an endorsement of the proposed transaction.
why_it_matters: Approval gives no comfort that the structure complies with insider trading law or the prohibited activities list; the executive bears that risk.

clause: Exceptions to this Policy will only be granted in exceptional circumstances. For example, where the ANZ Restricted Person is experiencing severe financial hardship or has an unanticipated significant financial commitment.
why_it_matters: A waiver of the margin/LTV financing ban for a routine funded collar is unlikely; the exception route is reserved for hardship and needs both Line Manager and Control Room approval.

clause: Key Management Personnel and Executive Directors may not enter into a transaction that operates to limit or reduce the economic risk of their shareholding below the minimum personal shareholding requirement.
why_it_matters: A collar (which limits economic risk) can only be written over shares held in excess of the executive's minimum personal shareholding requirement, so the collarable parcel must be sized after deducting the MSR.

clause: They can however enter into a transaction intended to hedge unrestricted Macquarie securities subject to pre-clearance and other general personal dealing requirements (and, in respect of Key Management Personnel, subject to section 2.4 below).
why_it_matters: The collar legs are expressly permitted over vested, unlocked shares with PTA pre-clearance in a Staff Trading Window; MEREP shares under holding lock or dealing restriction remain ineligible.

clause: Macquarie Staff who enter into margin loans or other financing arrangements over Macquarie securities should ensure they have sufficient available cash or other acceptable collateral to meet margin calls including during a period of extreme sudden market downturn.
why_it_matters: The loan leg secured on the collared shares is contemplated and not prohibited, but the executive is expected to be able to meet margin calls from other resources rather than by selling Macquarie shares.

clause: Liquidating a position to satisfy a margin call requires pre-clearance against Macquarie's PTA system.
why_it_matters: A lender's enforcement sale outside a Staff Trading Window would require pre-clearance that is only available in a window or under an exceptional-circumstances waiver, so the facility must not rely on forced sales of the collared shares.

clause: KMP must inform the Company Secretary immediately if ... the member of KMP holds Macquarie securities that have been lent, mortgaged, or charged to a financier; circumstances have arisen in which the financier is entitled or likely to become entitled to exercise a right under the finance arrangements to demand payment; the member of KMP expects that the demand will not able to be satisfied without the disposal of securities representing at least 1% of the total number of issued securities of Macquarie.
why_it_matters: Charging the collared shares to the bank triggers immediate notification to the Company Secretary (and likely ASX disclosure of the director's interest), and any LTV or event-of-default trigger must also be reported immediately.

clause: subject to Macquarie's discretion, a period of up to five weeks following the release of Macquarie's interim results (November/December), final results (May/June) and Annual General Meeting (July/August)
why_it_matters: Collar entry, any roll or reset, and unwind must each fall within one of three short discretionary windows a year, and the window may be shortened or withheld.

clause: All pre-clearances are subject to an expiry date and may be withdrawn if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances. A denied pre-clearance is final and binding on the Macquarie Staff member who made the request and must be kept confidential.
why_it_matters: The bank should expect that a cleared collar can be blocked before execution and that a refusal cannot be explained to it.

clause: Macquarie considers dealing to include, without limitation, securities transactions such as transfers of beneficial ownership and trading (either directly or indirectly), including entering into an agreement to trade.
why_it_matters: Signing the collar confirmation or any agreement to deliver shares is a dealing at signing, and any transfer of beneficial ownership to a lender or nominee is separately a dealing requiring pre-clearance in a window.

clause: Macquarie securities Includes, but is not limited to: ... Structured products providing exposure to MQG shares, including but not limited to ETFs; Futures contracts, options and warrants over MQG shares
why_it_matters: An OTC collar with a bank is a structured product providing exposure to MQG shares and is caught with no venue limitation.

clause: A waiver request must be submitted to RMG Employee Compliance in writing, accompanied by a statutory declaration from the requesting Macquarie Staff member declaring that: the proposed dealing is the only reasonable action available; they do not possess non-public price-sensitive information
why_it_matters: Out-of-window settlement, unwind or forced sale of the collared shares is available only through a hardship-style waiver at Macquarie's absolute discretion, which cannot be assumed in facility documentation.

clause: In the case of an on-market trade, the dealing occurs at execution (but not settlement) of the trade. In the case of an off-market trade, the dealing occurs at settlement of the trade. ... in the case of an off-market dealing, settle the dealing, in Wesfarmers or BWP Trust securities within two clear trading days of receiving confirmation from the Wesfarmers Company Secretary
why_it_matters: An OTC collar and secured loan are off-market dealings, so signing, funding and security grant must all settle within two clear trading days of clearance and outside a Blackout Period, which drives the execution timetable with the bank.

clause: Where any approval under this Policy is required for a dealing, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the 'front page' test.
why_it_matters: Even a policy-compliant collar can be refused if the Company Secretary considers the market would perceive it as an inappropriate use of position, so reputational optics of hedging director exposure are a live gating factor.

clause: the Corporations Act restricts directors and senior executives of the Wesfarmers Group who are classified as 'key management personnel' ... from entering into an arrangement (with anyone) if the arrangement would have the effect of limiting the exposure of that director or senior executive to risk relating to an element of that director or senior executive's remuneration that remains subject to restrictions on disposal. Clearance cannot be obtained ... for dealings which are restricted by the Corporations Act.
why_it_matters: The collar may only be written over shares that are both vested and free of any plan disposal restriction; vested shares still subject to a holding lock cannot be collared by KMP and no waiver is available.

clause: clearance can be given or refused at the discretion of the Wesfarmers Company Secretary, without giving reasons; clearance can be withdrawn by the Wesfarmers Company Secretary at any time prior to the order for dealing being lodged or otherwise authorised, if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances
why_it_matters: The bank should not price or commit until clearance is in hand, and the transaction can be pulled up to the moment of settlement.

clause: The only exception to the prohibition on dealing during Blackout Periods is a sale of Wesfarmers securities
why_it_matters: Entering, rolling, restriking or granting security under a collar can never occur in a Blackout Period; only a hardship or court-ordered sale, or a no-change-of-beneficial-ownership transfer, can be approved inside a blackout.

clause: in relation to Wesfarmers directors only, any other person or entity where dealing in Wesfarmers securities by that person or entity would require disclosure to the ASX by the Wesfarmers director. This includes where the Wesfarmers director: (i) controls the right to vote or dispose of Wesfarmers securities; or (ii) is entitled to benefit from a contract to call for, or deliver Wesfarmers securities.
why_it_matters: Routing the collar through a trust, company or superannuation fund does not avoid clearance, and the option contracts themselves are the type of interest that brings a vehicle into the director's Associated Party net.

clause: Directors and employees who acquire Wesfarmers securities under a Wesfarmers share plan must also comply with the rules of that plan when dealing in those securities.
why_it_matters: Plan rules (not in the policy) may impose holding locks or hedging bans over vested plan shares that would independently block a collar or security grant.

clause: Additional restrictions in this Annexure B apply to dealings in Wesfarmers and BWP Trust securities
why_it_matters: The clearance regime and Annexure B 9 restrictions extend to BWP Trust units, although the Blackout Periods are expressed to apply only to Wesfarmers securities.

clause: this does not include disposals of Wesfarmers securities within a short period of time after vesting or issuance of those securities under a share plan
why_it_matters: Newly vested shares can be sold or delivered under a collar without offending the three-month short-term rule, so the collar tenor need not be driven by the vesting date.

clause: This Policy applies to all of CSL's Personnel ... additional restrictions on dealing in CSL Securities which apply to Restricted Persons and their Related Parties
why_it_matters: The lodged document contains no definitions section, so whether a given executive is a Restricted Person or Global Leadership Group member, whether Related Parties include trusts and controlled companies, and whether CSL Securities includes OTC derivatives must be confirmed from CSL's internal definitions before structuring.

clause: Personnel must not obtain margin loans using CSL Securities (either solely or as part of a portfolio) as security for the loans, or enter into any other secured financing arrangements in respect of CSL Securities.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar secured on the collared shares is prohibited for every tier with no approval route, so only an unfunded collar could ever be considered.

topic: hedge exercise date in Open Period
clause: may hedge against vested CSL Securities that are not subject to a holding lock if the hedge is both initiated in, and arranged so that the specified exercise date falls within, an Open Period
why_it_matters: For eligible non-GLG Personnel, the collar's expiry or exercise date must be pre-set to fall within an Open Period, and an ad hoc Closed Period over that date requires approval to exercise.

clause: Hedging is a form of dealing ... Therefore, where hedging is not prohibited under this Policy it must be undertaken in accordance with this Policy.
why_it_matters: A permitted hedge still attracts Closed Periods, the three-month short-term rule and, for Restricted Persons, prior approval and the three-trading-day validity window.

clause: Unless otherwise notified to the Personnel, any dealing permitted under this section 2.7 Exceptional circumstances must comply with the other sections of this Policy.
why_it_matters: Hardship relief opens Closed Periods and the short-term rule only; it does not unlock hedging for directors and GLG or secured financing for anyone.

clause: If a request for approval to trade is granted, it may be withdrawn at any time prior to the order for dealing being lodged or otherwise authorised, if new information comes to light or there is a change in the circumstances of CSL Securities.
why_it_matters: Any cleared transaction can be pulled before execution, so the bank should not commit pricing until the order is authorised.

clause: Where any approval is required for a dealing under this Policy, approval may not be granted where the dealing may not satisfy the Front Page Test.
why_it_matters: Even a technically permitted hedge by a Restricted Person can be refused on reputational grounds without explanation.

clause: This Policy (except for section 3.1 Seeking prior approval) does not apply to: ... (c) transfers of CSL Securities resulting in no change in beneficial interests
why_it_matters: Even a transfer of shares to a custodian or nominee with no change in beneficial interest still requires the prior approval process for Restricted Persons.

clause: PDMRs are prohibited from undertaking any of the following Dealings with respect to Rio Tinto Securities: (a) Dealing in derivative products issued over or in respect of Rio Tinto Securities
why_it_matters: Both option legs of a collar are derivative products over Rio Tinto Securities, so no collar of any kind is available to directors, KMP or designated PDMRs, funded or not.

clause: (d) entering into margin lending or other secure financing arrangements in respect of Rio Tinto Securities.
why_it_matters: The loan leg secured on the collared shares is independently prohibited for PDMRs with no exemption authority.

clause: The following types of Dealings are excluded from the operation of this Policy and may be undertaken by Restricted Persons at any time, without prior written clearance ... (f) a disposal of Rio Tinto Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights.
why_it_matters: For non-PDMR Restricted Persons who lawfully grant security, the bank's enforcement sale is outside the Policy even in a Closed Period, though the Insider Dealing prohibition still applies.

clause: (e) entering into a transaction the economic outcome of which is dependent upon the price of a Rio Tinto Security, including but not limited to a transaction which has the effect of limiting the economic risk of holding a Rio Tinto Security
why_it_matters: An OTC collar with a bank is a Dealing regardless of venue or settlement method, so non-PDMR Permanent and Project Restricted Persons need prior written clearance for it.

topic: charge under derivative contract is dealing
clause: (h) entering into any margin lending, derivative contract or other secured financial arrangement pursuant to which a charge is granted over the Rio Tinto Securities.
why_it_matters: The security package of a funded collar is itself a Dealing, so the loan and charge must be cleared and executed inside the clearance window, not only the options.

clause: Rio Tinto prohibits Permanent Restricted Persons, from entering into arrangements which have the effect of limiting the economic risk related to an unvested share ... (or a vested share ... that is still subject to disposal restrictions).
why_it_matters: For non-PDMR Permanent Restricted Persons, only vested plan shares free of disposal restrictions, or non-plan shares, may be collared.

clause: must Deal in Rio Tinto Securities within the period specified in the written clearance to Deal, or in the absence of a period being specified, within two Business Days of the receipt of the clearance to Deal.
why_it_matters: The approver can grant a longer execution window, which may be needed to document an OTC collar and security, but the default is two Business Days (UK and Australian holidays both excluded).

clause: a company, trust, partnership or entity: which is managed by the PDMR or a family member; which is directly or indirectly controlled by the PDMR or a family member; which is set up for the benefit of the PDMR or a family member; or the economic interests of which are substantially equivalent to the PDMR's or a family member's.
why_it_matters: A collar or loan taken through a family trust or private company is a PCA Dealing needing clearance and immediate notification, and the PDMR bans on derivatives and secured financing apply to Dealing 'for the account of a third party, directly or indirectly'.

topic: post trade notification even if no deal
clause: After receiving the clearance to deal, if Restricted Persons decide not to deal in Rio Tinto Securities, you still need to submit a Post Trading Notification promptly, indicating that you did not deal
why_it_matters: A cleared but unexecuted collar still requires a portal notification.

clause: where exceptional circumstances, such as severe financial difficulty or compulsion by court order exist, which require an immediate sale of Rio Tinto Securities.
why_it_matters: Closed Period relief is confined to immediate sales, so collar entry, roll or unwind cannot be cleared inside a Closed Period.

clause: Transactions involving Woodside-based derivative securities by directors, executive key management personnel and other executives participating in an equity-based executive incentive plan, are also prohibited. ... Transactions in derivative securities include ... transactions in straddles or collars; and/or writing puts or calls.
why_it_matters: A collar is expressly named as a prohibited transaction for directors and executive plan participants irrespective of hedging purpose or vesting state, so no approval route exists for the option legs.

clause: directors or Company Secretaries of Woodside Energy Group Ltd and direct reports to the CEO are prohibited from pledging Woodside securities as collateral.
why_it_matters: The loan leg secured on the collared shares is independently banned for directors and the executive team, but not for GGC-nominated restricted employees or ordinary employees.

topic: exclusions carved back for directors in black-out
clause: Subject to the insider trading prohibitions outlined above, and other than in relation to dealings by Directors in black-out periods, the following dealings by a director or restricted employee are excluded from the operation of this Policy: ... disposal of Woodside securities as a result of a secured lender exercising their rights
why_it_matters: A secured lender's enforcement sale is outside the Policy for restricted employees, but for a director it would be a black-out period breach; the same carve-back applies to custodian or depositary transfers by directors in black-out.

topic: hedging vested holdings by restricted employees
clause: These requirements also apply to dealings in financial products issued by third parties in relation to Woodside securities which operate to limit the economic risk of a vested holding in Woodside securities.
why_it_matters: The Policy expressly contemplates restricted employees outside the section 5 tier hedging vested holdings with a bank product, on Compliance Certificate acknowledgement by the Group General Counsel within a 7-day window.

clause: Woodside will take a substance over form approach and will have regard to the intent and spirit of this Policy when applying and enforcing it.
why_it_matters: Restructuring a collar as a cash-settled swap, a funded forward or a family-trust transaction will be judged by economic effect against the derivatives, hedging and pledging bans.

topic: arrangements forcing disposal within three months
clause: you must not dispose of those securities or enter into arrangements (such as margin loans) which could result in those securities being disposed of within three months of acquisition.
why_it_matters: Even where financing is allowed, a loan or collar whose default or physical settlement could force delivery of shares acquired within the last three months is itself prohibited.

clause: A response would normally be expected within 24 hours ... Any such approval will be valid for 7 days from the date it is given
why_it_matters: Where a dealing is permitted, execution and settlement of documentation must fit in a 7-day window from approval or acknowledgement, and the approval can be conditioned or revoked before dealing.

clause: If any clearance, approval or acknowledgment is required for a dealing under this Policy, the clearance, approval or acknowledgement will not be granted if the dealing would not satisfy the Front Page Test.
why_it_matters: A hedge or financing by a senior person can be refused on perception grounds alone, without reasons.

clause: This Policy extends to all securities owned or controlled by a person covered by the Policy, whether those securities are held in the name of that person, in a company, through a trust, by a family member, by a friend or in some other entity or arrangement.
why_it_matters: Placing the collared shares in a trust, company or nominee does not take the collar or pledge outside the bans.

clause: Debt transactions that may be converted into Woodside shares are also prohibited by this Policy.
why_it_matters: A financing structured as an exchangeable or convertible instrument over Woodside shares is caught for the section 5 tier.

clause: A team member can only enter into a derivative contract that hedges their exposure to movements in the price of Securities if the exercise window for either party under that contract is not during a scheduled blackout period.
why_it_matters: The collar's expiry, exercise and settlement dates for both the executive and the bank must be scheduled outside the 30 June, 31 December and quarterly-update blackouts, which rules out American-style or early-termination rights exercisable in those windows.

clause: Where an unscheduled blackout period overlaps with an exercise period, a team member must not seek to exercise or settle the derivative and should inform the Company Secretary. A Committee of the Chairman, Group CEO and the Company Secretary will consider appropriate actions.
why_it_matters: The collar documentation needs a mechanism to defer exercise or settlement if an ad hoc blackout is declared, since the executive cannot settle and the outcome depends on a Committee decision.

clause: You are required to have sufficient resources to meet a margin call by means other than by a sale of your Goodman Securities.
why_it_matters: Any loan secured on the collared shares must be structured so that top-ups can be met in cash, since selling the shares to meet a call when trading is not allowed is a breach.

clause: If your margin lender sells any of your Securities at a time when trading is not allowed, it will be considered a breach of this policy. Any dealing in breach of this policy should immediately be disclosed to the Company Secretary for reporting to and consideration by the Board for possible disciplinary action.
why_it_matters: Bank enforcement rights over the collateral must be contractually suspended during blackouts and while the executive holds inside information, or the executive is exposed to disciplinary action.

clause: Key management personnel (as defined in the Corporations Act and included in the most recent Remuneration Report) must not have a margin loan in respect of Goodman Securities.
why_it_matters: 'Margin loan' is undefined; a bank loan secured on collared securities with a top-up mechanism is likely to be treated as one, so the funded leg is unavailable to directors and Remuneration Report KMP even though the derivative legs are permitted with consent.

clause: You must not trade the Securities until consent has been granted. Consent lasts 10 business days after which time you must again seek consent to trade. Consent may be withdrawn at any time before you trade in Securities if new relevant information becomes available or there is a change in circumstances.
why_it_matters: Entry into the collar and the loan must complete within 10 business days of consent, and consent can be withdrawn before signing.

clause: The arrangement must also comply with the law, the other provisions of this policy and any other conditions that you may be subject to (such as a minimum holding requirement).
why_it_matters: Shares subject to a minimum holding requirement may not be available to collar or deliver, and the bank should confirm whether hedged securities count towards that requirement.

clause: Special risks may arise where you do not have control of securities that may be acquired or sold in respect of which you have a beneficial interest. Care should be taken in relation to giving discretionary mandates where you have a direct or indirect interest in the securities, margin loans and derivatives
why_it_matters: Bank discretion to sell, rehypothecate or deliver collateral is flagged as a policy risk the executive bears.

clause: Their associates which include close family members and people or entities (such as family companies or self managed pension funds) where there is any influence over the investment process or where they are acting on behalf of the Director or employee.
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a family company or SMSF does not avoid consent, blackouts or the KMP margin loan ban.

clause: Consent is also not required where trading in Securities results in no change to the beneficial interest in the Securities
why_it_matters: Moving shares to the bank's custodian or nominee without change of beneficial interest needs no consent, though such 'trading' is not expressly excluded from blackout periods.

clause: A Designated Person must not enter into transactions which would have the effect of hedging or transferring the risk of any fluctuation in the value of ... Company Securities which are vested but still subject to a holding lock.
why_it_matters: Collared shares must be both vested and free of any plan holding lock; the bank should verify the lock status of each parcel before inception.

clause: To deal and dealing includes ... entering into agreements or transactions which operate to limit the economic risk of a person's holdings in Company Securities.
why_it_matters: The collar is a dealing in its own right regardless of venue or whether the OTC options are 'Company Securities', so Notification, the 7-day execution window and Prohibited Periods apply to inception, roll and unwind.

clause: derivatives and other financial products created by the Company or created or issued by third parties in relation to the Company's shares, debentures, options or other securities able to be traded on ASX or another stock exchange
why_it_matters: The 'able to be traded on ASX' qualifier could be read as limiting derivatives to exchange-traded products, but the economic-risk limb of dealing captures an OTC collar in any event.

clause: Notification means a notification in writing (including by email) that includes ... a confirmation that the Designated Person is not in possession of price sensitive information about the Company that is not generally available to the market.
why_it_matters: Outside Prohibited Periods no one approves the dealing; the executive self-certifies and must execute within seven days of the Notification, so the collar must be priced and signed inside that window.

clause: Closed Season means each of: (a) the period from the end of the financial year or half financial year to the business day after the time of release of the annual or half year results; and (b) the period from the end of the September quarter or March quarter to the business day after the time of release of the September or March quarterly reports.
why_it_matters: Quarterly reporting produces four closed seasons per year plus Board blackouts, narrowing the windows for inception, roll, unwind and physical settlement of the collar.

topic: prohibited period relief is disposal only
clause: may be given written clearance to sell or otherwise dispose of (but not purchase) Company Securities during a Prohibited Period
why_it_matters: Buying back the written call or purchasing a put to unwind or restructure during a Prohibited Period cannot be cleared even in hardship; only a disposal (e.g. delivery of shares on call exercise) could be.

clause: Designated Persons must refrain from dealing in Company Securities during Prohibited Periods.
why_it_matters: There is no carve-out for a lender's enforcement sale or for physical settlement at expiry, so a bank enforcing its security or exercising the call in a Closed Season could put the Designated Person in breach; expiry dates and enforcement mechanics should avoid Prohibited Periods.

clause: Short Term Dealing includes dealing in Company Securities within a 3 month period
why_it_matters: A collar with a tenor under three months, or an unwind within three months of inception, risks characterisation as Short Term Dealing; tenor should exceed three months.

clause: If a Designated Person may not deal in Company Securities, he or she must take all reasonable and necessary steps to prevent any dealing in Company Securities by Related Parties unless the Designated Person has complied with this Policy on behalf of that Related Party.
why_it_matters: A collar entered through a family trust or controlled company requires the Designated Person to make the Notification on the Related Party's behalf and observe Prohibited Periods.

clause: A director is required to notify the Company Secretary if there is any change in the director's relevant interest in securities of the Company ... with sufficient notice to allow the Company Secretary to make the necessary notifications within 5 business days after the change occurs.
why_it_matters: The collar and the security granted to the bank will be disclosed to ASX via Appendix 3Y, so the arrangement will be public within five business days.

clause: Subject to paragraph 21, if you're a Designated Person, you are prohibited from entering into any hedging arrangement that limits the economic risk of holding Telstra securities.
why_it_matters: The collar (purchased put plus written call) is itself a hedging arrangement over vested shares and is banned for every director, executive KMP and their Closely Related Parties regardless of vesting state.

clause: using Telstra securities as collateral in any financial transaction, including entering margin loan arrangements in respect of Telstra securities or transferring Telstra securities to an existing margin loan account
why_it_matters: The loan leg secured on the collared shares is independently prohibited for Designated Persons, so both halves of a funded collar fail.

clause: Despite paragraph 16, if you entered an arrangement prior to becoming a Designated Person that would otherwise be prohibited under paragraphs 16 b)-d), you are permitted to continue that arrangement for 12 months from the date that you became a Designated Person or until the date of expiry of the relevant arrangement, whichever occurs earlier.
why_it_matters: A collar loan put in place before appointment as a Designated Person can run for at most 12 months after appointment; the hedge leg has a separate, Company Secretary-approved 'limited period' under paragraph 21.

clause: If you have any hedging arrangements in effect prior to becoming a Designated Person that would otherwise be prohibited under paragraph 19, you may, in certain limited circumstances with the approval of the Telstra Company Secretary, be permitted to continue such arrangements for a limited period.
why_it_matters: Continuation of an existing collar after appointment is discretionary and time-limited, so the bank cannot assume the hedge survives the client becoming a Designated Person.

clause: a disposal of Telstra securities as a result of a secured lender exercising their rights pursuant to an arrangement that was permitted under paragraph 17
why_it_matters: Lender enforcement is an excluded dealing only for grandfathered pre-appointment arrangements; there is no carve-out for any other enforcement sale, and directors must notify the Company Secretary before relying on it.

clause: In exceptional circumstances, you may be granted approval to deal in Telstra securities in a way that's prohibited under this Policy ... where the Exceptional Dealing Approval Request is accompanied by sufficient evidence that the proposed dealing in Telstra securities is the only reasonable course of action available in the circumstances
why_it_matters: The only theoretical route to a funded collar for a Designated Person is a hardship-type approval showing the collar is the only reasonable course, which is unlikely for a discretionary monetisation.

clause: Buying and selling Telstra securities within a 3-month period and entering into short term arrangements such as forward contracts in respect of Telstra securities will always be considered speculative dealing and accordingly is prohibited.
why_it_matters: Even a non-hedging restructure using a forward is deemed speculative, closing off prepaid-forward alternatives to a collar.

clause: can be withdrawn at any time before you deal if new information becomes available or there is a change in circumstances ... Any such refusal is confidential and you must not disclose the fact that your request has been refused to any other person without the consent of the Telstra Company Secretary.
why_it_matters: Where any approval is obtained, the bank may not be told of a refusal or withdrawal, and the executive must execute within 2 business days.

clause: The trustee of a trust or fiduciary arrangement of which you or any of the persons referred to in (a) or (b) are a beneficiary
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a family trust, controlled company or a trust of which the executive is a beneficiary does not escape the hedging and collateral bans.

clause: The Telstra CEO and Group Executives should undertake any dealings in Telstra securities in compliance with the minimum shareholding requirement (MSR) set out in the Minimum Shareholding Requirement Policy
why_it_matters: A separate MSR policy may treat hedged or encumbered shares as not counting toward the holding requirement; it should be reviewed alongside this Policy.

clause: You must not deal if your proposed dealing could be perceived by the market as you taking advantage of your position in an inappropriate way.
why_it_matters: Applies to everyone including non-Designated staff, so even a permitted collar for a Band C executive must survive a market-perception test.

clause: where any Telstra securities granted to a Designated Person under an equity plan cease to be held under the terms of that plan (for example, Telstra securities that are acquired following the exercise of options or rights or that are released from restriction), the Designated Person must only deal in those Telstra securities in accordance with this Policy
why_it_matters: Vested plan shares become ordinary holdings subject to the full hedging and collateral bans once released, so there is no plan-based carve-out for collaring them.

clause: enter into arrangements to use Woolworths Securities as collateral in any financial transaction following the date of this Policy (no new margin lending arrangements)
why_it_matters: A loan secured on the collared shares is a new arrangement using Woolworths Securities as collateral and is prohibited for Specified Persons and their Closely Related Parties, so only an unfunded collar is available; the ban is prospective, so pre-20 August 2021 facilities appear grandfathered.

clause: derivatives within the meaning given in section 761D of the Corporations Act (such as options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps and collars); and any other transaction in financial products that operates to limit the economic risk associated with holding the relevant securities.
why_it_matters: A collar is expressly a Derivative and therefore a Security and a Trade, so it is squarely within the clearance, Blackout Period and section 3.4 regimes regardless of OTC form.

clause: enter into hedging arrangements in relation to vested and unrestricted Woolworths Securities (no hedging) without first obtaining clearance in accordance with section 4.3.
why_it_matters: The option legs over vested unrestricted shares are permissible with prior written clearance, although the '(no hedging)' label signals approvers may be reluctant.

clause: Trade, Trading includes ... creating a security interest or other financial interest over Securities, engaging in any transaction involving a change in beneficial ownership of the Securities
why_it_matters: Granting security to the bank or transferring shares to a custodian or the bank would itself be a Trade needing clearance and barred in Blackout Periods, in addition to the collateral ban.

clause: Any Specified Person, or any Closely Related Party to a Specified Person, who wishes to trade in Woolworths Securities at any time must seek prior approval in writing from the relevant approver in Schedule 1.
why_it_matters: Clearance is required outside Blackout Periods too, so inception, roll, unwind and physical settlement of the collar each need fresh written clearance valid for five business days.

clause: Woolworths may also publicly disclose any Derivative positions over Woolworths Securities taken out by a Woolworths Group Director. These disclosures may be made irrespective of whether or not they are technically required by the ASX Listing Rules or the Corporations Act.
why_it_matters: A director's collar may be announced to the market at Woolworths' discretion even where no Appendix 3Y obligation arises.

clause: Provided a Trade is placed and executed by you or your broker prior to the commencement of a Blackout Period, it is not a breach of this Policy if the Trade settles and clears after the commencement of a Blackout Period.
why_it_matters: A collar executed before a Blackout Period may settle inside it, but option expiry or exercise falling within a Blackout Period is not covered by this relief.

clause: Trade in Woolworths Securities during designated Blackout Periods (closed periods)
why_it_matters: There is no carve-out for a lender's or counterparty's enforcement or physical settlement in a Blackout Period, and the hardship exception requires clearance and a demonstrated absence of any other reasonable option.

clause: Woolworths Team Members must not sell Woolworths Securities within 3 months after their purchase
why_it_matters: Shares bought within the past three months cannot be delivered under the call, and a collar unwound quickly may be characterised as speculative Trading.

clause: family trusts or superannuation funds where the Specified Person is a trustee, beneficiary or an advisor to the trustee
why_it_matters: Structuring the collar or loan through a family trust, SMSF or family company does not escape the collateral ban or the clearance requirement.

clause: If the market was aware of all the current circumstances, could the proposed Trading be perceived by the market as me taking advantage of my position in an inappropriate way? How would it look if the Trade was reported on the front page of the newspaper?
why_it_matters: Approvers may apply a reputational filter to an executive collar independent of the technical rules.

clause: You are prohibited from engaging in any speculative transactions involving ResMed Securities, including: Buying or selling puts or calls on ResMed Securities
why_it_matters: A collar is a purchased put and a written call, so both option legs are expressly prohibited for Insiders regardless of whether the shares are vested, the venue is OTC, or the purpose is protective rather than speculative.

clause: any transaction involving ResMed Securities (including any option exercise, stock purchase, stock sale, gift, loan, pledge, hedge, contribution to a trust, or any other transfer or acquisition), must first obtain pre-approval of the transaction from the Global General Counsel
why_it_matters: Pledging shares to the bank and any non-option hedge are clearable transactions for Specified Persons, so the loan leg is possible with approval even though the option legs are not; approval must be sought at least two business days ahead.

clause: Approval for a proposed transaction may be withheld ... if ... the transaction could result in adverse publicity or have a material adverse impact on trading in ResMed Securities or ResMed; for persons subject to Section 16 ... the transaction could result in liability to the Specified Person under the short-swing rules of Section 16(b); or sufficient advance notice had not been given to allow preparation and review of a Form 4
why_it_matters: Even a permitted pledge or hedge can be refused on reputational or Section 16(b) grounds, and a refusal cannot be overruled by management.

clause: Clearance, when given, will be only for the precise period specified. ... It is incumbent on the Specified Person to stop any such order that extends beyond the permitted period, or when the Specified Person comes into possession of material non-public information.
why_it_matters: Any cleared transaction must be executed within the stated period and abandoned if inside information arises, so a multi-step financing cannot rely on a standing approval.

clause: You are prohibited from placing any "stop loss" orders or any other "limit order" involving ResMed Securities, except pursuant to a qualified Rule 10b5-1 plan
why_it_matters: Price-triggered mechanics such as knock-outs, automatic top-up sales or lender liquidation instructions could be characterised as prohibited stop-loss or limit orders unless housed in a pre-approved 10b5-1 plan.

clause: Apart from these five exceptions, listed in a through e of this paragraph, there shall be no exceptions to the foregoing prohibitions.
why_it_matters: There is no hardship, court-order or lender-enforcement relief, so any sale or settlement outside a trading window is a breach.

clause: Total sales of ResMed common stock by a covered individual for any three-month period may not exceed the greater of: (i) 1% of the total number of outstanding shares ... or (ii) the average weekly reported volume ... The shares must be sold either in a "broker's transaction" or in a transaction directly with a "market maker."
why_it_matters: Physical delivery of shares to the bank on exercise or enforcement by a director or executive officer is an affiliate sale subject to Rule 144 volume limits, manner-of-sale rules and Form 144 filing.

clause: require our Section 16 Persons to report all transactions involving ResMed Securities (including options, warrants, and other "derivative securities") to the SEC. Almost all transactions must be reported within two business days after the transaction date.
why_it_matters: Any derivative or pledge-related transaction by a director or executive officer becomes public on Form 4 within two business days and may be matched against other trades within six months for short-swing profit disgorgement.

clause: you could receive permission to buy a security, but later be refused permission to sell it (at least temporarily). These situations are frequently beyond the control of ResMed, and could lock you into an unwanted investment for a considerable period of time.
why_it_matters: ResMed disclaims responsibility if a later clearance to sell or unwind is refused, so the executive bears the liquidity risk of being unable to settle or restructure.

clause: An Employee includes an Employee's spouse, children, or relatives in the same household; corporation or other business entity controlled by an Employee, or trust in which the Employee acts as trustee or has a beneficial or pecuniary interest.
why_it_matters: Structuring a collar or loan through a family trust or controlled company does not escape the puts and calls ban or the pre-approval requirement.

clause: this policy may be amended or supplemented at any time by our Global General Counsel, Chief Executive Officer or Chief Financial Officer and that any such amendments or supplements will become effective immediately.
why_it_matters: The rules governing an outstanding financing can change without notice or Board process during the life of the arrangement.

clause: You will only be allowed to purchase or sell ResMed Securities during a trading window period commencing one (1) full trading day following the date of our public disclosure of the financial results
why_it_matters: Section 5 does not say whether it binds all Employees or only Insiders, but for directors and executives it plainly applies and the Global General Counsel may refuse clearance whenever the window is not in effect.

clause: In accordance with Listing Rule 12.9, which is due to take effect from 1 January 2011, we submit a copy of the Company's current Insider Trading Policy.
why_it_matters: This is the December 2010 lodgement of a May 2010 policy; the current ResMed policy should be checked before relying on these terms.

clause: Directors, members of the Executive Committee and their Related Parties must not enter into hedging arrangements in relation to Transurban Securities.
why_it_matters: The option legs of a collar are a hedging arrangement and are absolutely prohibited for directors, Executive Committee members and their Related Parties over vested and unvested securities alike.

clause: Employees must not obtain margin loans using Transurban Securities (either solely or as part of a portfolio) as security for the loans, or enter into any other secured financing arrangements in respect of Transurban Securities.
why_it_matters: A loan secured on the collared shares is prohibited for every Employee and Related Party, so a funded collar fails for all tiers regardless of whether the hedge itself is permitted.

clause: may hedge against vested Transurban Securities that are not subject to a holding lock if the hedge is both initiated in, and arranged so that the specified exercise date falls within, an Open Period.
why_it_matters: For Employees below Executive Committee level an unfunded collar must be executed in an Open Period with a fixed expiry inside an Open Period, which effectively requires European-style options and rules out American exercise or early termination rights that could fall in a Closed Period.

clause: Hedging is a form of dealing. Therefore, where hedging is not prohibited under this Policy it must be undertaken in accordance with this Policy.
why_it_matters: A permitted hedge by a Restricted Person needs prior approval, is subject to Closed Periods and must be reported to the Company Secretary within two ASX trading days as a 'hedge'.

clause: Where an Employee ... has a hedge which is to be exercised in an Open Period but the Transurban Board has decided to declare or extend a Closed Period to cover the exercise date, the Employee may request prior approval to exercise
why_it_matters: Settlement of a permitted employee hedge can be blocked by a later Closed Period and depends on discretionary approval, a risk the bank should price into settlement mechanics.

clause: I will not engage in short selling of Transurban Securities, obtain margin loans using Transurban Securities (either solely or as part of a portfolio) as security for loans or enter into any other secured financing arrangements in respect of Transurban Securities.
why_it_matters: Every approval request requires a personal undertaking against secured financing, so a funded collar would involve a false acknowledgement as well as a policy breach.

clause: a person or company that has a private understanding or business arrangement with the person for dealing in Securities
why_it_matters: A counterparty or vehicle with a standing arrangement to deal in Transurban Securities on the executive's behalf may itself be a Related Party, so the bans cannot be avoided by interposing an entity or nominee.

clause: If a request for approval to trade is granted, it may be withdrawn if new information comes to light or there is a change in the circumstances of Transurban Securities. If a request for approval to trade is refused, the decision is final and binding and the Employee who has sought the clearance must keep the information (of the refusal) confidential
why_it_matters: Any approved dealing can be revoked before execution within its five-trading-day validity and the executive may not tell the bank why a request was refused.

clause: may be granted prior approval to sell or otherwise deal in Transurban Securities during a Closed Period or on a short term basis
why_it_matters: Closed Period relief extends to any dealing, not just sales, but is confined to hardship, court order or other exceptional circumstances and cannot override the hedging or secured financing bans.

clause: the shares in THL, the shares in TIL and the units in THT stapled together and quoted on the ASX; and any other Securities relating to Transurban.
why_it_matters: Any hedge or security would need to cover the stapled triple security as a unit, and 'any other Securities relating to Transurban' sweeps in OTC option contracts.

clause: Employees must not, except in exceptional circumstances (see section 5.7), deal in Transurban Securities during the following periods (Closed Periods)
why_it_matters: There is no carve-out for a counterparty's enforcement or physical settlement in a Closed Period, so even a permitted employee hedge must avoid settlement or unwind in the 1 July and 1 January Closed Periods.

clause: Aristocrat will take a substance over form approach and will have regard to the intent and spirit of this Policy when applying and enforcing it.
why_it_matters: A bank loan secured on collared shares with LVR triggers or lender sale rights risks being treated as a 'margin lending arrangement' banned for Designated Persons even if not so labelled.

clause: Designated Persons must not: (a) enter into a margin lending arrangement in respect of Aristocrat securities; or (b) transfer securities in Aristocrat into an existing margin loan account.
why_it_matters: The ban is confined to margin lending; a fixed-term, non-margin secured loan is not expressly prohibited, so the loan leg turns on whether the facility has margin-call mechanics.

clause: Hedging includes entering into any arrangements that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding Aristocrat securities.
why_it_matters: A collar is squarely hedging, so it is barred over unvested plan securities and shares under a holding lock, and permitted only over vested, unrestricted shares.

clause: Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 3-month period and entering into other short-term dealings (for example, forward contracts).
why_it_matters: A collar with tenor under three months or early-termination features may be characterised as a short-term dealing; tenor should exceed three months.

clause: Where any approval is required for a dealing under this Policy, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the Front Page Test.
why_it_matters: Approval of a collar over executive shareholdings is discretionary and may be refused on reputational grounds alone, without reasons.

clause: The approver is not obliged to provide reasons for any aspect of their decision, and may revoke their approval at any time. If a request is not approved or an approval is revoked, that fact must be kept confidential.
why_it_matters: A cleared collar must be executed within 5 business days and approval can be withdrawn before signing; the bank cannot be told why.

clause: A request for approval under sections 4.2 or 4.3 by members of the Executive Steering Committee must be accompanied by a confirmation that the member is in compliance with the Executive Minimum Shareholding Policy.
why_it_matters: ESC members must show MSR compliance before a collar is approved; whether collared shares count toward the MSR is governed by the external policy.

clause: a company or any other entity which the Designated Person has an ability to control.
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a controlled entity or family trust does not avoid the approval requirement, blackouts or the margin lending ban.

clause: Buy or sell orders for Aristocrat securities which are placed but not completed outside of a blackout period ... must be completed within 5 trading days of the order being placed otherwise it will lapse; and the order cannot be varied.
why_it_matters: Physical settlement or unwind of a collar that straddles the start of a blackout is not accommodated; settlement dates should avoid blackout periods.

clause: Any person who breaches this Policy could face disciplinary action (including forfeiture of securities and/or suspension or termination of employment).
why_it_matters: A breach caused by the collar or the lender's enforcement could result in forfeiture of the collared securities, a risk to the bank's collateral.

clause: Restricted Persons must not trade in Company Securities at any time, including in the exceptional circumstances referred to in Section 6, unless the Restricted Person first emails a Securities Trading Policy Request Form to the Approving Officer, copied to the Company Secretary, and obtains written clearance to trade
why_it_matters: Every leg of a collar (entry, roll, unwind, physical settlement) is a trade needing fresh written clearance, valid for 5 business days unless the Approving Officer sets another period.

clause: Restricted Persons must not enter into margin loan agreements or other secured lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities without first obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer
why_it_matters: The loan leg secured on collared shares is expressly permitted subject to clearance, so the funded collar has a policy pathway.

clause: a disposal of Company Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement
why_it_matters: A bank's enforcement sale is carved out of the blackout restrictions in Section 5, though the carve-out does not in terms extend to the Section 7 clearance requirement; enforcement remains subject to insider trading law.

clause: Written clearance under this Policy may be withdrawn by the Approving Officer in writing, in person or by email at any time during the clearance period ... should the Approving Officer consider that circumstances have changed, having regard to the broader reputational, governance and other implications of the proposed trading
why_it_matters: A cleared collar can be blocked before execution on reputational grounds, so pricing and signing should follow promptly after clearance.

clause: the Approving Officer must obtain advice from General Counsel, and may as appropriate seek input from other relevant Key Management Personnel and Senior Employees about the broader reputational, governance and other implications of the proposed trading
why_it_matters: Clearance for hedging a director's holding is discretionary and reviewed for governance optics, and cleared trades are reported to the Board quarterly.

clause: derivatives of any of the above (including equity swaps, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options) whether settled by cash or otherwise
why_it_matters: An OTC put and call with a bank, cash or physically settled, is squarely a Company Security and each is a trade requiring clearance.

clause: an unlisted body corporate which the Key Management Personnel, Senior Employee or Key Consultant or Key Contractor controls or is director of, a trust of which [they are] a trustee and of which he or she or any of the persons referred to above is a beneficiary
why_it_matters: A collar or loan entered by a family trust or controlled company must be cleared as if by the Restricted Person.

clause: Restricted Persons must not disclose to anyone that an Additional Period is in effect.
why_it_matters: The executive cannot tell the bank why a settlement or unwind is delayed, so the collar documentation should accommodate undisclosed trading suspensions.

clause: The Company Secretary must report all notifications of trading in, and clearances given, in relation to trading in Company Securities at the next Quarterly Board meeting of the Company.
why_it_matters: A cleared collar and secured loan will be reported to the full Board, so confidentiality from the Board cannot be assumed.

clause: derivative ... includes options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps, collars and any other transaction in financial products that operates to limit the economic risk associated with holding securities.
why_it_matters: A collar is expressly a derivative and a risk-limiting transaction, so it is caught by the absolute hedging ban with no room for characterisation arguments.

clause: Hedging of QBE securities by a Relevant Person and their Closely Related Parties is prohibited at all times.
why_it_matters: The put and call legs are prohibited for all tiers over vested and unvested shares alike, and the paragraph 5 waiver power does not extend to hedging.

clause: pledging, collateralisation, or use of QBE securities as security for any other financing arrangement.
why_it_matters: The loan leg secured on the collared shares is expressly not permitted regardless of whether the facility has margin-call mechanics.

clause: entering into margin lending, stock lending or other financing arrangements related to securities; ... granting a mortgage or other right over securities to another party; and transferring legal ownership of securities
why_it_matters: Even an unsecured financing referenced to QBE shares, or a transfer to a custodian or bank nominee, is a dealing subject to Closed Periods and clearance.

topic: no waiver for hedging or financing
clause: the Relevant Person may apply to the person(s) listed in the table below (Assessor) for a waiver from compliance with the provisions of that paragraph [4.2(a) or 4.2(b)].
why_it_matters: Exceptional-circumstances waivers cannot unlock a collar or secured loan; only Closed Period and short-term dealing relief is available.

clause: Where this Policy requires a Relevant Person to do something (e.g., obtaining clearance in accordance with paragraphs 5 or 6), that person must also do so for their Closely Related Parties.
why_it_matters: Structuring the collar through a spouse, controlled company or family trust does not escape the hedging and secured financing bans.

clause: Any person who is proven to have breached this Policy could face disciplinary action (including forfeiture of QBE securities and/or suspension or termination of employment).
why_it_matters: Forfeiture of QBE securities is a stated sanction, so collateral pledged in breach of the Policy is at risk.

clause: Transactions effected through employee share plan administrators or platforms are considered dealings in securities for the purposes of this Policy.
why_it_matters: Delivering vested plan shares to a bank via the plan administrator is itself a dealing requiring clearance.

clause: All directors, Restricted Persons and their Connected Persons are prohibited from obtaining a margin loan using the Company's securities (either solely or as part of a portfolio) as security for the loan or entering into any secured financing arrangement in respect of the Company's securities.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, secured on the collared shares, is prohibited for every Restricted Person regardless of whether the facility has margin-call mechanics.

clause: For the avoidance of doubt, such dealings include: ... selling securities in the Company to satisfy a call pursuant to a margin loan.
why_it_matters: A Restricted Person cannot themselves sell to meet a lender's call; only a disposal effected by the secured lender exercising its own rights is an excluded dealing under 7(g), so any facility would have to rely on lender enforcement rather than borrower top-up sales.

clause: disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights.
why_it_matters: Enforcement sales by a lender are outside the blackout, clearance and short-term rules, though subject to insider trading law; this carve-out sits uneasily with the ban on entering the secured financing in the first place.

topic: hedging ban for directors and ELT
clause: All directors, members of the Executive Leadership Team and their Connected Persons are prohibited from hedging their exposure to Company securities.
why_it_matters: The put and call legs are barred outright for directors and ELT over any Company securities, vested or not, with no waiver route.

clause: any Permitted Restricted Person must not enter into, renew, alter or close out a hedge transaction when they are in possession of Inside Information
why_it_matters: For GM-level executives an unfunded collar is possible, but every roll, amendment or unwind is itself a cleared dealing that cannot occur while holding Inside Information or in a blackout.
